the development of novel spintronic devices based on current-induced spin-orbital magnetic fields (SOT).
the detection of current-induced magnetic fields by means of time resolved magneto-optical microscopy.

we have demonstrated a new method to determine the magnitude as well the symmetry of current induced spin-orbit magnetic field in a ferromagnetic/non-magnetic metal system.
the proposed approach is a phase independent method to determine the magnitude and symmetry of the current induced SOF.

this work provides a phase-independent and self-calibrating approach for the determination of SOFs in current induced spin-orbit torque devices, which is applicable to a wide range of materials systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed an efficient and phase independent method to determine the magnitude and symmetry of the current induced spin-orbit magnetic field (SOF).
we present a novel method to detect current induced spin-orbit magnetic field in a phase independent manner.

we have developed a new approach to detect the current induced spin-orbit magnetic field in ferromagnetic metal/semiconductor heterostructures by measuring the mode patterns of spin wave modes excited by the current.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SOFs can be determined directly by analyzing the SSW mode patterns, without a need for lineshape fitting.
it is possible to extract quantitative information about the SOFs from the shape of the spin waves, which opens up a novel avenue to study the SOFs in spintronic devices.
it is possible to detect the SOFs in the presence of a microwave current without the need for a static magnetic field.
